articles.content:
The Bay Area Women’s Open will bring together 161 women cricketers from more than 15 U.S. states and Canada across nine teams during Labor Day Weekend 2026, as the tournament enters a new phase under the Bay Area Open Cricket Platform.  
![](https://usacricketers.com/uploads/b19c8819190b_1788529924.jpg)  
The event, originally launched as the Blazers Bay Area Open by Bay Blazers in 2024, will be staged for a third consecutive year with the Bay Area’s three Minor League Cricket organizations — Bay Blazers, Silicon Valley Strikers and San Ramon Grizzlies — joining forces with the Northern California Cricket Association (NCCA) and Major League Cricket’s San Francisco Unicorns.  
  
The tournament will feature four teams in the Elite Division and five in the Premier Division. The Elite field will include two East Coast and two West Coast teams, while the Premier Division will feature teams representing the Southwest, Northwest, Central and Eastern regions.  
  
The player pool includes approximately 30 cricketers who have represented the United States or Canada at senior or age-group international level. More than 80 others have experience in the USA cricket pathway at intra-regional, regional or zonal levels.  
  
That mix is expected to provide emerging players with the opportunity to compete alongside established international cricketers and players who have progressed through the national pathway.  
  
Matches will be played at Taarika Cricket Ground, Wilson Cricket Field in Santa Clara, Easterbrook Cricket Ground in the Moreland School District and Ortega Cricket Field in Sunnyvale.  
  
The collaboration marks a change from the tournament’s original structure, with the participating organizations seeking to connect grassroots cricket, academies, clubs, NCCA competitions, Minor League Cricket and Major League Cricket around a broader pathway for women and girls.  
Biju Nair, founder and CEO of Bay Blazers, said the decision to expand the initiative was driven by the desire to build a sustainable pathway rather than simply enlarge an individual tournament.  
  
“Having Bay Blazers, Silicon Valley Strikers and San Ramon Grizzlies standing together, with NCCA and the San Francisco Unicorns supporting this initiative, sends an important message to every young girl playing cricket here,” Nair said.  
  
Silicon Valley Strikers CEO Jayanth Chakraworthy said the Bay Area possessed the talent and infrastructure to become a major center for women’s cricket in the United States, while San Ramon Grizzlies CEO Samir Shah described collaboration as a way to create opportunities that would be difficult for a single organization to provide independently.  
  
NCCA president Prakash Giri and San Francisco Unicorns CEO David White also expressed support for creating stronger opportunities for women and young players in Northern California.  
  
The 2026 tournament therefore represents more than the third edition of an established competition. It is the first major expression of the Bay Area Open Cricket Platform’s longer-term objective of connecting young players with youth, pathway, domestic and international cricket.  
  
For the tournament, the expansion creates a broader North American platform for women’s cricket while bringing multiple levels of the Bay Area cricket structure together under one initiative.

articles.content:
**Sham Ali  
Celebrating 47th Anniversary –20260830. Match #1390**: - Cosmos return to old familiar grounds at Westbury High school in awe of the transformation and beautification that have transpired over the years that lends to a more accommodating atmosphere. A ground which Cosmos had battled some of their fiercest competitors and enjoyed some of their best years of playing cricket in the Metropolitan Cricket League in the eighties and nineties. On this occasion, with a new look young Cosmos team ran into a powerhouse Westbury team and was awakened to some quality cricket. That was, by any measure, a far cry from that which they were engaged in over the last few years, actually, there is very little comparison.  
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Doneshwar Dayanand (left) and Hemraj Bhimchan. Photos by Sham Ali**  
  
Devindra Balgobin did that which he has been doing all season in the New York National Cricket League, led his team with determination and a calm head to the semi finals, and with a weakened outfit for this new venture, the challenges were real. He won the toss and elected to bat, but when he looked around the ‘elements’ were conveniently missing. So like any good soldier he took the responsibility of leading from the front and got padded up to open the batting. Wow, captain doing his thing by taking the responsibility of leading his team.  
  
Unfortunately, when he did so in the last match of the preliminary rounds and again in the quarter finals where he dug his team out of a hole from 42 for 5, with a defining inning that ultimately won the match, he was chastised for it by the usual tainted tongues. At the time, he would have ponder that the collective decisions were honest, thoughtful and purposeful towards in an attempt to weed out some of the indiscipline that have sprouted up from mimi cliqueism. However, it was anything but, and that was met with a level of absolute ignorance that was deafening. It appeared, in some minds, that rudeness and disrespect is acceptable if it is your friend that is committing the act. Sadly, that behavior has become prevalent in this day throughout this cricket community from the top to the bottom, and appeared to be the norm.  
  
We were pleasantly entertained by some of that behavior at our independence match, a behavior which no self-respecting individual would condone, but self-respecting and unruliness don’t often find common ground, and however, nothing should be surprising thereafter. As if that was not enough, most recently, we were again rudely blindsided by similar behaviors from the most unlikely of sources which leaves a lot to be desired. Who knows else is coming down the pipe.  The legend Bob Marley said it best in some powerful lyrics ‘Man to man is so unjust, children. You don't know who to trust. Your worst enemy could be your best friend. And your best friend your worst enemy. Some will eat and drink with you. Then behind them su-su 'pon you…And who the cap fit. Let them wear it’.   
  
You never know these days in this doggy dog cricket circle where the hand is outstretched looking for handouts wherever and whenever it is available. And oh, just in case you missed it and is wondering, what the hell, well this is recreational cricket in NY for you. I do not want to imagine what would happen if the stakes were a little higher as a dollar. Some things never change, they say. While these issues in clubs created an unhealthy environment, in most cases, it is an ingrained behavior fostered by some who gloat and enjoyed it. So, let’s ignore the mediocrity and mute the noise, and rise above this pettiness. The club has been be better for it on every occasion, but that is a story for another day, and so much for this digression.  
  
On this occasion Balgobin rallied with his team like he has always done.  Ahmad Dodson (9) was looking quite comfortable in his new role but ran out himself when he ambled out of his crease.  Nazim Ally (0) suffered the same. Sunil Narine (0) was undone by an unusual creeper that reared in from wide of the off-stump and crashed into his stumps. Commander Frahan (0) had to retire hurt after he suffered a blow on the cheek that looked extremely dramatic on film, but apparently, he got some glove on it. He is fine, but a helmet at all times is absolutely necessary. Balgobin (9) went via lbw. Doneshwar Dayanand (1) took a blow to the chest and ‘the general’ just brushed it off, he is rock solid you know, he is in the gym pumping iron.   
  
Hemraj Bhimchan (0) made his debut into the big league and missed a Yorker. The left-handed youth-man Suhail Lalmahamad (0) got a good in-swinger, while yours truly S. Ali (2) took his fair share of the short stuff with some ease on the face of the bat, not sure why. But some unkind souls may challenge their imagination to enjoy the view. Oh, how I wish. It was Sher who said ‘if I could turn back time’. That will never happen so knock yourself out today young man, because this same willow that attracted the attention of a few of these opponents minutes ago, would have landed those short stull on the trees over the square-leg boundary, like so many others did. But this is a new day many many years later. Westbury pace attack was simply overpowering for this Cosmos line-up as evidenced by a paltry 30 in 10.4 overs. J. Brown took 3 for 5, and S. Hackett 3 for 4.  
  
Westbury made light work of a small total but not before Cosmos struck a few telling blows. Dodson in his first over clipped the edge of S. Williams, but the man behind the stumps apparently did not hear, and stood unmoved with no finger movements. In the next over, Narine also clipped the edge of Williams (23), but Doneshwar said that the shopkeeper was asleep (he is taking a lot of shots at the captain). Dodson then bagged three quick wickets with a brilliant piece of swing bowling in his second over.  With his first ball, he pierced the gates and cleaned up the left-handed D. Beckford (8) with a good in-swinger.   
  
With his second, he picked the outside edge of D. Duncan (0), and ‘lord have mercy’ Balgobin with the glove pulled off a one-handed stunner diving to his right, and hit the ground hard with tremors of 5.999 on the Richter scale. He took a while to get up. Excellent catch budday! Dodson was on a hat-trick but it was not to be. He struck again with his sixth ball when N. Rambarose (0) played down the wrong line to another out-swinger that crashed into his back leg. And for as long as it last, it was a day that defines Cosmos in more ways than one, torrid and rewarding, and enjoyable.   Westbury raced to a 7-wicket victory. A. Dodson took 3 for 7.

articles.title: Kingsmen Xi Win Nyncl Division 1; Everest/acs Lift Premier Title
articles.excerpt: The victorious Kingsmen XI celebrate with the championship trophy after their historic NYNCL Division 1 triumph. Kingsmen XI were crowned NYNCL Division 1 champions after bowling M
articles.content:
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**The victorious Kingsmen XI celebrate with the championship trophy after their historic NYNCL Division 1 triumph.**  
  
Kingsmen XI were crowned NYNCL Division 1 champions after bowling Melbourne CC out for just 10 runs, while Everest/ACS continued their remarkable run of success by winning the Premier Division title in a dramatic double-header of finals at Baisley Pond, New York.  
  
Kingsmen XI posted 181 for 5 from their 25 overs after Melbourne CC won the toss and elected to bowl. Arnil Ragdnath led the batting effort with 61, striking five fours and a six, and shared a 66-run opening partnership with Kyle Kowlessar, who contributed 30 off 30 balls.  
  
Viendra Gooniah then provided the late acceleration, smashing 54 from only 30 deliveries, with five fours and two sixes, to push Kingsmen XI to a formidable total.  
  
Melbourne's reply quickly turned into a rout. Captain Moien Khan and Ansaar Yasim dismantled the batting order with outstanding spells. Khan returned figures of three wickets for three runs from five overs, including three maidens, while Yasim claimed four for three from five overs, with two maidens.  
  
Yasim was named Final MVP for his match-winning performance.  
  
Melbourne CC were dismissed in the 11th over for 10, with Safdar Khan and Khomal Sookram making two runs apiece as their top scorers. Kingsmen XI therefore secured the championship by 171 runs, completing one of the most one-sided finals in NYNCL history.  
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Everest/ACS poses for a team photo after securing victory in the NYNCL Premier Division final.  
**  
In the Premier Division final, Everest/ACS defeated New York XI after choosing to bowl first following the toss.  
  
Keon Lake spearheaded the bowling attack with five wickets, finishing with 5 for 30 from 4.3 overs. Damion “Jazzy” Jacobs added two wickets for 27 runs from six overs as Everest/ACS restricted New York XI to 174.  
  
Karan Ganesh top-scored for New York XI with 29, while Randall Wilson made 28 and Akshay Homraj contributed 24.  
  
Everest/ACS then produced a controlled chase, led by Bhaskar Yadram's 67 from 41 balls. Patton Jr added 33 from 26 deliveries, while Oraine Williams scored 34 to guide Everest/ACS to the target and another Premier Division championship.  
  
The title capped another successful stretch for Everest/ACS, who had won the Metropolitan League Sunday 40-over championship just a week earlier. Their back-to-back titles across different competitions and formats underline the team's consistency and depth.  
  
For Kingsmen XI, the Division 1 triumph marks a historic championship built around a powerful batting effort and extraordinary bowling display. Everest/ACS, meanwhile, strengthens its position among New York's leading teams with another trophy. Both results underline the growing competitiveness and depth of New York club cricket.

articles.title: Unicorns Sport Foundation Awards $50,000 Grant To California Cricket Academy
articles.excerpt: San Francisco, September 2, 2026 — The Unicorns Sport Foundation, the charitable arm of Major League Cricket franchise San Francisco Unicorns, has awarded a $50,000 infrastructure
articles.content:
**San Francisco, September 2, 2026** — The Unicorns Sport Foundation, the charitable arm of Major League Cricket franchise San Francisco Unicorns, has awarded a $50,000 infrastructure grant to the California Cricket Academy (CCA) and named the Bay Area nonprofit a strategic community partner.  
  
The foundation also confirmed the appointment of former Meta global policy chief Monika Bickert to its board of directors.  
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Former Meta global policy chief Monika Bickert has joined the Unicorns Sport Foundation’s Board of Directors.**  
  
The grant to CCA, an organization that has worked in Bay Area cricket development since 2003, will fund facility upgrades and youth programming. Organizers said the investment is intended to help community hubs serve more than 1,000 young players annually through coaching, leagues and other programs.  
  
The partnership sits within the foundation's stated targets of engaging over 10,000 young people and delivering 100 community programs across the Bay Area by 2030, built around three priorities: closing cricket's gender gap, addressing structural barriers to access, and building grassroots pathways and infrastructure.  
  
"The Unicorns Sport Foundation exists to use cricket as a tool to create meaningful and lasting opportunities for young people," said Joydeep Ganguly, the foundation's chairman. "California Cricket Academy has spent more than two decades building those connections, and their commitment to community, player development, and accessible facilities makes them an ideal partner."  
CCA president Hemant Buch said the grant represented "an investment in our shared vision of creating world-class community cricket facilities and expanding opportunities for every child to learn, play, and thrive through cricket."  
  
Bickert's board appointment adds a senior corporate and legal profile to the foundation's leadership group, which already includes Ganguly, Unicorns co-founders Anand Rajaraman and Venky Harinarayan, and Unicorns chief executive David White. Bickert spent more than a decade in senior roles at Meta, most recently overseeing global policy management, and previously worked as a federal prosecutor. A Harvard Law School graduate, she is set to join the university's faculty this fall as the Steven and Maureen Klinsky Visiting Professor of Practice for Leadership and Progress.  
  
"Cricket is particularly well positioned \[to unite communities\], because it is fast-growing and accessible for newcomers of all backgrounds," Bickert said of her appointment.  
  
White welcomed the addition, saying Bickert's experience "will be invaluable as the Foundation enters an exciting phase of growth," adding that the board is "exceptionally well positioned to deepen the Foundation's impact" going forward.

articles.title: India To Host Inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 In Mumbai And Vadodara
articles.excerpt: The International Cricket Council (ICC) today announced that the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 will be staged in the Indian cities of Mumbai and Vadodara from 14 to 2
articles.content:
The International Cricket Council (ICC) today announced that the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 will be staged in the Indian cities of Mumbai and Vadodara from 14 to 28 February.  
  
The Cricket Club of India (CCI) in Mumbai and the Vadodara International Cricket Stadium will be the venues for the landmark tournament that will bring together six of the world’s leading women’s cricket teams - Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka.  
![](https://usacricketers.com/uploads/f329e3ec2ae8_1788372597.jpg)

**India will host the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in February of 2027.**  
  
Those six teams, who qualified as per their positions in the ICC Women’s T20I Team Rankings on the 6 July qualification cut-off date, will compete in a round-robin league, with the top two sides advancing to the final on 28 February.  
  
The tournament was originally scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka but will now be staged in India as Sri Lanka Cricket continues to make the requisite reforms outlined at the ICC’s Annual Conference in July.  
  
The ICC assessed three candidates - Bangladesh, India and South Africa - against its established host evaluation criteria before recommending India as the replacement host, a decision ratified by the ICC Board on 2 September.  
  
ICC Chairman, Mr. Jay Shah, said: “The ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket. As the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage.  
  
“With a marquee ICC women’s event now taking place every year, we have a significant opportunity to build greater momentum, provide more consistency and create a stronger rhythm for the women’s game, its players and its fans around the world."

articles.title: Cricket Hall Of Fame Marks 45 Years With 2026 Induction Class
articles.excerpt: The Cricket Hall of Fame will mark 45 years of recognizing contributions to cricket when it stages its 45th induction ceremony on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel i
articles.content:
The Cricket Hall of Fame will mark 45 years of recognizing contributions to cricket when it stages its 45th induction ceremony on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at the Marriott Hotel in Windsor, Connecticut.  
  
The ceremony will honor 14 inductees in the Class of 2026, with Dennis Heath receiving the Lifetime Achievement Award and Rajeev Puthenveetil of Primrose Cricket Club being presented with the President Award. Una Clarke and Yvette Clarke will receive Certificates of Appreciation.  
![](https://usacricketers.com/uploads/006b6de989f7_1788276145.jpg)

**Here are four members of the Class of 2026 inductees (l-r), Ajith Bhaskar, Hemant Buch, Kinjal Buch and State Rep. Bobby Gibson.**  
  
The Cricket Hall of Fame was established under the Sportsmen’s Club in 1980, with its first induction ceremony held in 1981 in Hartford, Connecticut. It describes itself as the world's first Cricket Hall of Fame and operates as an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.  
  
Over 45 years, the organization has recorded 323 heroes, 342 awards, 252 inductees and 73 international inductees. Its honors also include 11 Lifetime Achievement Awards, 179 other inductees and 70 Presidential Awards.  
  
The Lifetime Achievement Award is the Hall's highest honor and is presented to existing Cricket Hall of Famers whose contributions have had a lasting impact on cricket.  
  
Among those who have received the award are Sir Garfield Sobers, Sir Michael Holding, Jatin Patel, Roy Reid, Muhammed Qureshi, Ivy Mahabir, Clarence Modeste, Denzil Powell, Lloyd Dixon, Tony Becca and Roy Sweeney.  
  
The Hall's list of honorees includes some of the most prominent figures in international cricket. Australia is represented by Sir Donald Bradman, Kerry Packer, Greg Chappell and Reginald Leslie, while England's inductees include Sir Leonard Hutton, Freddie Trueman, Tony Greig and Brian Close.  
  
India's notable inductees include Sunil Gavaskar, Gundappa Vishwanath, Bhagwat Chandrasekhar, Dilip Vengsarkar, Ajit Wadekar, Farouk Engineer, Chetan Chauhan and Syed Abid Ali. Pakistan's list features Hanif Mohammad, Wasim Akram, Zaheer Abbas, Younis Khan, Mushtaq Mohammad, Moin Khan and Abdul Razzak.  
  
The West Indies contingent includes Sir Garfield Sobers, Michael Holding, Sir Vivian Richards, Sir Andy Roberts, Alvin Kallicharran, Sir Clive Lloyd, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Courtney Walsh, Sir Richie Richardson, Joel Garner, Desmond Haynes, Gordon Greenidge and Sir Hillary Beckles.  
  
The Class of 2026 comprises Mark Azeez, Kumar Balakrishnan, Ajith Bhaskar, Hemant Buch, Kinjal Buch, Leslie L. Clarke Sr., Henry Forde, State Rep. Bobby Gibson, Patrick Hamilton, Howard Johnson, Rick Nugent, Jay Singh (CT), Steve Stephenson and Francis Trevor of Sierra Leone.  
  
The October ceremony continues an annual tradition dating to 1981, when the Hall began formally recognizing individuals for their contributions to the sport. The organization also maintains a museum featuring cricket memorabilia, exhibits and historical accounts.  
  
The 2026 ceremony will extend that tradition into a 45th year, adding a new group of honorees to an institution that has recognized cricket figures from the United States and around the world.

articles.title: Minor League Cricket 2026 To Begin September 17, Playoffs Set For Houston
articles.excerpt: Minor League Cricket will return September 17 for its 2026 regular season, with 62 matches scheduled across eight US venues before the October playoffs in Houston. File photo court
articles.content:
![](https://usacricketers.com/uploads/a76c17af3887_1788008921.jpg)

**Minor League Cricket will return September 17 for its 2026 regular season, with 62 matches scheduled across eight US venues before the October playoffs in Houston. File photo courtesy of Andy Mead/YCJ**  
  
Minor League Cricket (MiLC) will begin its [2026 regular season](https://www.minorleaguecricket.com/MiLC/schedules?leagueId=4gjH8PVcUeCazKJUkOOrOA&year=2026&series=Blc41vvV_UlHFvY3oOajUg&division=all&day=All+days&seriesName=MiLC+2026) on September 17, with 62 matches scheduled across eight venues in the United States before the playoffs and championship final move to Houston in October.  
  
The regular season will run through September 27, followed by a scheduled break before the postseason takes place at Prairie View Cricket Complex (PVCC) from October 21-25.  
  
The gap in the calendar has been designed to allow MiLC players to take part in the ICC Cricket World Cup League Two matches at Grand Prairie Stadium in Texas and the Atlanta Open, avoiding clashes with the decisive stages of the domestic competition.  
  
The 2026 season was originally scheduled to begin on August 7. The revised September start is intended to align venue availability, broadcasting and team logistics across the league's participating markets.  
  
Matches will be played at eight venues nationwide, including Church Street Park in Morrisville, North Carolina, Grand Prairie Stadium in Texas and the newly opened Knight Riders Cricket Ground in California.  
  
The process of building the league's rosters began on Friday, August 28, with the MiLC Divisional Drafts taking place on a staggered schedule.  
  
The draft will retain the league's snake format, with the lowest-ranked teams from the 2025 season receiving the first selections in their respective divisions. Results are expected to be announced within 24 hours of each draft's completion.  
  
Teams can pass on selections during the divisional draft and will have the opportunity to sign eligible players as free agents once all divisions have completed their selections, subject to league roster regulations. Each team must carry between 14 and 18 players.  
  
The 2026 campaign will also see a change in team ownership and identity, with All Stars Dallas replacing Kings XI Dallas following a change in ownership ahead of the season.  
  
MiLC regular-season matches will again be open to spectators free of charge. Matches will also be available through MLC Network for viewers in the United States and internationally.  
  
The league's 2026 schedule includes the regular-season fixtures as well as information on team rosters, live scores, match scorecards and competition updates.  
  
The revised calendar gives MiLC a concentrated 11-day regular season before the October postseason. With the league break accommodating international and domestic commitments, the 2026 playoffs and championship final will determine the season's champion at Prairie View Cricket Complex from October 21-25.

articles.title: Ny Xi Crush 592 Cricket Academy As Everest/acs End Kingsmen’s Winning Run
articles.excerpt: Damian Jacobs (left) produced a match-winning spell of 4 for 25, while Oraine Williams (right) struck an unbeaten 80 to guide Everest/ACS into the NYNCL Saturday Premier Division f
articles.content:
![](https://usacricketers.com/uploads/da0a4df3f793_1787666722.jpg)

**Damian Jacobs (left) produced a match-winning spell of 4 for 25, while Oraine Williams (right) struck an unbeaten 80 to guide Everest/ACS into the NYNCL Saturday Premier Division final.**  
  
NY XI and Everest/ACS will meet in the NYNCL Saturday Premier Division final after contrasting semifinal victories on August 22, with NY XI defeating 592 Cricket Academy and Everest/ACS ending Kingsmen XI’s three-game winning streak.  
  
At Baisley Pond, 592 Cricket Academy won the toss and elected to bat, but the decision quickly backfired as they were bowled out for 54 in the 24th over. Kellon Carmichael top-scored with 17 from 35 deliveries, but the rest of the batting order struggled against a disciplined NY XI attack.  
  
Dino Chooweenam led the destruction with a five-wicket haul, finishing with 6 overs, including one maiden, for just 11 runs. Marvan Prashad was equally effective, taking three wickets in his six overs while also conceding only 11 runs, including one maiden.  
  
NY XI had little trouble chasing the modest target, reaching the required total in under 10 overs for the loss of one wicket. Jamal Norton top-scored with 26, while Randal Wilson remained unbeaten on 19. Fifteen-year-old Shawn Ishmael was the only 592 bowler to take a wicket, finishing with 1 wicket for 3 runs from his lone over.  
  
The second semifinal at Roy Wilkins produced a more competitive contest, although Everest/ACS ultimately secured a comfortable victory over Kingsmen XI.  
  
After winning the toss, Everest/ACS elected to field and reduced Kingsmen to 71 for 5 in the 15th over. Kevin Christian helped steady the innings with 36 from 35 balls, while Viendra Gooniah contributed 22. Kevin Augustin then provided the late impetus, striking 47 from 43 deliveries to lift Kingsmen to 134.  
  
Everest/ACS's bowling was led by former Jamaica national team and CPL player Damion “Jazzy” Jacobs, whose six-over spell produced four wickets for 25 runs, including a maiden. Gavan Brown and Keon Lake claimed two wickets apiece as Kingsmen were restricted to a manageable total.  
  
The chase was effectively settled by a 125-run opening partnership between Amarnauth Persaud and Oraine Williams. Persaud made 39 from 50 balls, while Williams carried his bat for an unbeaten 80.  
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Kingsmen XI’s Kevin Augustin’s all-round effort went unrewarded as he scored 47 and claimed 2 for 25 in the semifinal defeat to Everest/ACS.**  
  
Kevin Augustin, who had earlier made 47 with the bat, was Kingsmen’s most successful bowler, taking 2 wickets for 25 runs from five overs. However, he could not prevent Everest/ACS from completing the chase at 136 for 2 in 19.4 overs. Kwame Patton Jr. finished the match with a flourish, scoring 10 from three balls.  
  
Reflecting on Kingsmen XI’s second season in the NYNCL Premier Division, founder and captain Daryl Heerasingh said: “Last year we were eliminated in the first round. This year we came one step closer to a final. Hats off to Everest/ACS—their players and management have been dominating cricket in New York for a very long time. Winning is what they do best. We played this game as if it were a final, and ACS came out on top.”  
  
Kingsmen will now turn their attention to the club’s youth team, which will contest the morning final on Saturday. NY XI and Everest/ACS, meanwhile, will meet at Baisley Pond on August 29 with the Saturday Premier Division championship at stake.

articles.title: Cosmos Defeated Eagles And Into The Semi Finals
articles.excerpt: By Sham Ali Celebrating 47th Anniversary –20260816. Match 1387): - Throughout the season, he has been bombarded with the tease especially from his manager Dooneshwar as to when wil
articles.content:
**By Sham Ali  
Celebrating 47th Anniversary –20260816. Match #1387): -** Throughout the season, he has been bombarded with the tease especially from his manager Dooneshwar as to when will he show up with the bat. Well, Captain Devindra Balgobin could not have chosen a more crucial match to put a lid on the noise and saw his team turned in an excellent all-round performance last Sunday at Baisley Cage against Eagles in the quarter finals and booked a spot in the semis.   
  
Eagles had the better of Cosmos in their last encounter in the preliminary rounds, but Cosmos was up to the task in this ‘do or die’ quarter finals match-up. Balgobin won the toss and elected to bat under overcast conditions. They found themselves in some serious trouble after their top order wobbled, and the ball didn’t even touch the grass as yet, and both openers, Antanio Rooplall and Yogeshwar Ramgobin, were back in the pavilion by the third over courtesy of a swipe and a heave that leaves a lot to be desired in such a crucial match. It did not get any better as Eagles bowling attack held a tight line. Ghanam Tariq and Vian Gooniah tried to repair the inning, but that was short-lived when Gooniah played back to a short ball that skidded through and cleaned him up, Tariq followed in similar fashion soon after. Akash Rahim didn’t used up any ink when chased a wide delivery, not sure what else he was chasing, and found the man at backward point.   
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Captain Devindra Balgobin led the batting charge with a superb 45. Photo by Sham Ali**  
  
At that stage, Eagles had their claws firmly fixed on Cosmos with the score on 42 for 5 in the 13th over, but Captain Devindra Balgobin walked in under pressure, walked in with Eagles swarming, but found a way to stand firm and dug his team out of a hole and put them into a commanding position. Actually, Balgobin found himself padded up by the fifth over instead of his usual twenty fifth over during the season where swinging for the hills was the route. However, this was new territory, and he adapted perfectly to his role. Additionally, that role was equally shared by Inzy Khan. Khan who announced his intentions with a thumping six over extra-cover and followed up with a few telling blows was a clear indication that this pair was prepared for the battle.   
  
However, batting on this pitch with an unpredictable bounce and a heavy outfield would require grit and application to score runs. Unfortunately, a combination of poor pitches has tested the mental fragility of many. Khan though, appeared to gather strength in the challenges of these conditions as stroked the ball with authority. He drove high and hard and cleared the mid-off boundary with an air of arrogance while Balgobin played within his limitations and worked the field. He waited for the opportunity and timely launched onto paceman Sachin Lakhan for two dismissive maximums over mid-on and mid-wicket as he and Khan dragged their team out of a hole and took control of the inning. They proceeded to construct a crucial 6th wicket partnership of 60 runs after the initial implosion and brought a sense of calm to the proceedings. That partnership shifted the momentum ever so slightly to Cosmos side. With the score on 102 for 6 in the 23rd over, Khan on 27 tried to ‘up the tempo’ but succeeded in picking out the man on the deep mid-on boundary.  
  
Cosmos batting has depth, and two defining cameos for Govin Persaud and Ahmad Dodson in the closing overs yielded 63 runs in the last 7 overs pushed Cosmos to a competitive total.  Persaud played the shot of the day when he unleashed a crisply timed drive to the extra-cover boundary to open his account, and followed up with a maximum over mid-on. He eventually holed out on the mid-wicket boundary for a 13-ball 23 runs. Dodson has been in this situation from the very first match of the season and has delivered on very occasion. When Balgobin on 45 flicked to the man on the mid-wicket boundary with the score on 148 for 7, he had delivered a captain’s inning of substance, and placed his team in a good position. Dodson then took control of the closing overs to push Cosmos to a competitive total of 166 for 9 in their allotted 30 overs. V. Persaud took 2 for 20, S. Lakhan 47 and M. Mangaroo 2 for 37.  
![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

**Izzy Khan delivered an ideal all-round performance, chipping in with a valuable 27 and picked up 2 for 26. Photo by Sham Ali**  
  
In their reply, Eagles got off to an aggressive start as they dealt in boundaries, but Cosmos kept calm amidst the flurry of boundaries. Ryan Ganesh has been bowling well throughout the season, and again in this match. He initiated the breakthrough when he pierced the defense of S. Mohammed (9) with a japper and uprooted his middle stump. Dodson then handed S. Khan (12) a peach of an out-swinger that clipped the off bails. Ganesh then followed up with another good delivery that jagged back to remove W. Ward (6). But Eagles kept fighting with M. Verasammy taking full advantage of the power-play overs and finding the boundaries with regularity. He launched into Inzy Khan's first over with three consecutive boundaries that included two maximums off the first three balls to move to 29 runs, and then in the fourth ball, he offered a dolly to Ramgobin at extra-cover that went in and out.  
  
Despite, Eagles losing wickets at regular intervals, they kept scoring at a healthy nine runs per over with Verasammy firing on all cylinders. However, Balgobin knew his plan and stuck to it. Verasammy did not relent on his aggressive intent and decided to live by the sword against Thakoordeen. Thakoordeen has been crafty in his spell and should have picked up Verasammy in his previous over had Vian held on when he ran in and cover good ground from point and dove forward but it spilled out, however, in his next over he induced an aggressive stroke from Verasammy who he swung hard to the mid-wicket region, but got a leading edge that flew high into the air and headed towards Thakoordeen. He settled under it, hands by his side, his legs doing the jiggy dance, and eyes to the skies. Was he looking at the ball or offering a silence prayer, lord help me please, this is not happening, perhaps having flashbacks from the last match when he spilled a similar catch and the batsman went on to score a century. Lo and behold, his prayers were answered. Thank you, Lord! Entered the savior, Govin, who was in hot pursuit and shouted leeeeave, and gloved the catch quite comfortably, 84 for 4 in 10.4 overs   
  
That was a vital wicket and the crucial breakthrough for Cosmos. Balgobin pounced on the opportunity to tighten the screws on the opposition with Govin leading the chorus non-stop, and suddenly Cosmos boys were in on every ball, and the pressure was mounting. That resulted in two brilliant run outs. M. Kallicharran slashed to backward point was intercepted by Ghanam Tariq who then executed and brilliant play when he sent the perfect throw to Govin to run out a scrambling R. Doordarshan (0), 85 for 5 in 12.5 overs, and Cosmos smelled blood and and targeted the jugular. Thakoordeen then had J. Ramkaran (4) take quite comfortably by Rooplall at deep mid-on, 100 for 6 off 16.5 overs.  
  
Balgobin seems to pull all the right moves in this match from the beginning to the end as he marshalled his team. On his return, Inzy Khan, immediately got into the wickets column when he struck twice in one over. He uprooted Kallicharran (23) middle stump and had D. Hibbert taken by who else, Thakoordeen, on his second try, he must be taking his que from yours truly, 116 for 8 in 21.4 overs. S. Lakhan (1) then pushed to point region and took off, the ball got stuck in the grass with Govin in pursuit, he picked up and ‘shy-down-the-stump’ leaving Lakhan scrambling hopelessly ‘miles’ away, and fittingly, Ganesh returned and drove the final nail to give Cosmos a comprehensive 38 runs victory and a spot in the semi finals. R. Ganesh took 3 for 24, I. Khan 2 for 26, T. Thakoordeen got 2 for 30.

articles.title: Crucial Times Await Sachin
articles.excerpt: Sachin Tendulkar is accustomed to enduring scrutiny of the meanest type from the world’s best bowlers. But within eight weeks he will encounter an examination unusual for cricket s
articles.content: Sachin Tendulkar is accustomed to enduring scrutiny of the meanest type from the world’s best bowlers. But within eight weeks he will encounter an examination unusual for cricket stars. Opposing teams, fans and the media will have all eyes and lenses on the great man as cricket’s biggest competition comes to town to the West Indies. It will not be for Tendulkar’s looks — everyone knows he exhibits minor physical change from the time he debuted 17 years ago. Nor will it be an examination of his marital life — the world knows he has a solid relationship with wife Anjali and their two kids. Rather Tendulkar will be under the microscope for doing the things that made him a legend from Bombay to Bridgetown — that of scoring runs. Those who admire him will be happy if he finds his best form before the first World Cup delivery is sent down in Jamaica’s Sabina Park. Those who worship him might have to be placed on suicide watch if he does not set the spanking new stadiums ablaze there. And even those who support non-India teams will be disappointed if he does not get among the runs, in what could be his World Cup swansong. The cause for the abnormal attention on the Bombay mega-star needs little justification. Ever since his return to competition last year from a string of injuries Tendulkar has not been himself. He has not dominated bowlers the way he used to that yielded him more than 10,000 Test runs, more than 14,000 One Day runs with 35 and 40 centuries respectively in both forms of the game. It is said that injury and age is a telling combination for sportsmen after years of wear and tear. And already the whispers are making the rounds surrounding the Indian batting sensation ever since elbow and shoulder problems forced him to miss in total a, year of competition between 2005 and 2006. Disgruntled Indian fans accustomed to him reeling off ton and ton with the ease they exhibit in downing a cup of tea, did the unimaginable in the crucial return series against Pakistan last year. Boos rang out from the stands at Amedabad after one of frequent low scores from the country’s greatest batsman which staggered the rest of the world, and enticed one of India’s leading newspapers to question Tendulkar’s presence in the team . “Endulkar”? was a headline never thought possible in the heyday of Test cricket’s leading century maker, yet India’s decline since the departure of coach John Wright only bolstered the local media’s confidence to diss the country’s most acclaimed cricketing son. Whether it shook the great man’s resolve only time will tell, but the statistics state Tendulkar’s scoring has not improved since then. India lost both the Test and One Day series heavily against Pakistan when he returned from a second absence for the shoulder injury last year. They were embarrassed in the Invitational limited overs series the India Board hosted for Australia and West Indies in Malaysia and despite a big 141 against West Indies from the master, it was just not enough. Another first round elimination in the Champions Trophy staged in India, placed greater pressure on the former world number two ranked team, in which their mega batsman’s non scoring malaise deepened. And when they toured South Africa last month Sachin ‘s two half centuries was all he mustered in all of three Tests and four One Day Internationals that culminated in a crushing defeat and a heart wrenching 2-1 Test loss respectively. At the same time Tendulkar’s main batting rival in the fans minds, Brian Lara continued to make the headlines with centuries against Pakistan that landed him one away from the former’s Test record. Lara is not motivating his West Indies team to any significant level of success in the Test arena, but he is ensuring his batting legacy will be unforgettable when he eventually quits the scene. And that will not be anytime soon, as even at 37 he is yet to contemplate a retirement date. Tendulkar also had to hear Shane Warne and Glen McGrath rate the triple world record holder Lara, their most difficult batting foe, long after Muttiah Muralitharan made an identical pronouncement. Then former Test stars Ian Chappell, Tony Greig, Ravi Shastri, Wright and Sanjay Manjrekar, adjudicated Lara the best contemporary batsman, in a Cricinfo convened panel, based on his consistency through a 16-year international career. Although Tendulkar has never shown any interest in the bragging rights game between himself, Lara and Australia captain Ricky Ponting, all the recent putdowns must be tough to take. After all he is human. Whether all of it, or some of it ignites the competitive fires within the Mumbia Maestro, the world will know within a week. Tendulkar and Lara will suit up for their respective countries in another of the numerous pre-World Cup warm-up competitions the India board has arranged for its team. The venue will be India and Tendulkar will have an attack he is familiar with and from which he reeled off his biggest ODI score in recent times. If the upcoming four-match series doesn’t bring out the best in him, don’t expect it to happen in the World Cup. Stay tuned.

articles.title: Dr Toppin’s Curious Wicb Snub
articles.excerpt: Strange things occur in cricket, but none are more inexplicable than those that surface from the West Indies Cricket Board. The latest is the abrupt decision by the Board’s new Chi
articles.content: Strange things occur in cricket, but none are more inexplicable than those that surface from the West Indies Cricket Board. The latest is the abrupt decision by the Board’s new Chief Executive Officer-designate to decline the position before starting. Dr Roland Toppin was supposed to occupy the head chair from February 1 to fill the position left by Roger Braithwaite after almost one year. Now two weeks prior, the WICB is left in a tailspin and ruing the prospect of another difficult search for its leading executive officer. Whatever the reasons for Toppin’s sudden decision, it does little to enhance the WICB’s already battered reputation or his either. For an individual with heavy credentials he has been exposed as seriously indecisive or was otherwise taken for a ride by the Board and decided to jump ship in frustration. With the WICB’s poor track record one gets the impression it is the latter. In the run-up to his appointment Toppin had professed his love for West Indies cricket. He said he played seriously and wanted to become a Test player like most young West Indians at the time. Now, having the opportunity to be involved in an important way, Toppin grabbed the opportunity with both hands, and possibly accepted without having all the loose ends tied. But enthusiasm don’t always get in the way of professionalism. And Toppin having worked in the hierarchy of a leading University here in the U.S, must be a stickler for standards and principle. The Board has not been a crusader in either, hence Toppin is history where they are concerned now. The fact that several top employees have quit the Board in recent times says a lot about its operations. The public is well aware of it through the WICB’s messy handling of its teams. The inner workings are now gradually beginning to take shape from the outside. The loss of Michael Hall, Leonard Robertson and most recently Zoral Barkley is telling it all. One needs no more evidence to deduce the perilous state of the West Indies Cricket Board. Fortunately Clive Lloyd, one of the team’s best ever captains, seems prepared to lend a helping hand. Currently development committee head, and having acted as consultant and now manager for the team on tour, one hopes his presence will make a difference to the wobbly administration. He did thus with the team in the 1970’s and now has a chance to make history repeat itself. Is Sarwan fit or not? Given his importance to the West Indies team, it is difficult to fathom the West Indies Cricket Board’s dubious handling of Ramnaresh Sarwan’s instep injury. Presently the team is India for World Cup warm-up games without its vice captain. It was stated he was unfit for selection, but lo and behold, the public was informed yesterday he would be suiting up for Guyana in the Carib Cup, one day before the India series starts. If there ever was a conflict of interest, this development beats all, more so since both competitions are under the Board’s jurisdiction. From all indications Sarwan was supposed to be recovered by now since incurring the injury early December. If he is good enough to play for Guyana then the same should apply for West Indies duty, which is ostensibly more important. An urgent WICB explanation is therefore required on whether the player is ready or not for competition.

articles.title: Eaca Re-elects Rudy Persaud President
articles.excerpt: With the holidays now past and the winter season dwindling down, the eyes of cricket lovers are trained on the 2010 cricket season. It has been nearly five months since cricketers
articles.content:
With the holidays now past and the winter season dwindling down, the eyes of cricket lovers are trained on the 2010 cricket season. It has been nearly five months since cricketers and cricket spectators have been to the cricket parks around the New York area. They are all now bursting with anxiety and anticipation of the start of another season of their summer sport. Administrators of the various cricket leagues are also looking forward to the 2010 cricket season. \[caption id="attachment\_366" align="alignright" width="172" caption="Rudy Persaud was re-elected as president of the Eastern American Cricket Association for another year. (Photo by Shiek Mohamed)"\][![](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Rudy_Persaud1-172x300.jpg "Rudy_Persaud")

](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Rudy_Persaud1.jpg)\[/caption\] The leagues have been holding meetings and making all the other necessary preparations for, as they hope, another successful few months of cricket. The 2009 season gave endless enjoyment and fulfillment to nearly all who are connected to the sport. It is with this feeling of excitement that the "boys of summer" and their followers are anticipating the coming cricket season. The Eastern American Cricket Association was one of the leagues that called its Annual General Meeting in preparation for 2010. This was done on Sunday, January 31st, at the Naresa Palace on Rockaway Boulevard in Richmond Hill, New York. Eleven clubs out of the fourteen member-clubs were represented at the AGM. The gathering discussed the 2009 season, carefully analyzing the things that went wrong and the things that should have been done; in general some shortcomings. Among those were complaints from a few clubs that the league’s administration showed a bias against certain clubs. Notably, a club complained that on one particular Sunday it rained continuously from daybreak, resulting in the president calling off six matches. However, one of the scheduled matches was not called off. The complaint was that by not calling off that match the president favored one club who would gain some ground on another club, which was leading the favored club by one point, at the time. Another complaint was that it took the league nearly five months to address a protest filed by one of its affiliate clubs. Again, the allegation of favoritism was suggested. After tying up the league’s 2009 business, the officers vacated their posts and elections for the 2010 slate of officers were held. The Secretary of the United States of America Cricket Association, Mr. John Aaron, served as the Returning Officer. I must say that he conducted the balloting in a very efficient and democratic manner. President Rudy Persaud was reelected to his position as head of the organization, beating out a challenge from his 2009 VP Colin Sandy. This would be Mr. Persaud’s third stint in that capacity. Bayshore Tigers’ Qasim Butt was elected Vice President, over runner-up Colin Sandy. Richmond Hill’s Sunesh Wazid was reelected Secretary unopposed. The Treasurer’s post was filled by Victory Cricket Club’s Sumit Rajpaul unopposed. Everest/ACS’ Zamin Amin was elected Assistant Secretary/Treasurer over Hillside’s Zaman Juman. It was very noticeable that during the elections some politicking was going on. The election, however, was a fair one. The new slate of officers was installed in to their posts by the Returning Officer. Before relinquishing his chair Mr. Aaron cautioned the new officers about the burden of responsibility resting on their shoulders. "You came from five different clubs," Aaron warned, "but now you do not represent your club, you represent all the clubs." Krish Prasad, the Region's representative on the USACA board of directors, thanked all the officers for their willingness to serve, and for the sacrifice that they will be asked to make. He reassured all that he is convinced, "…the EACA is the best league in the New York metropolitan area, despite what bad things some people may be writing about us.” The newly installed officers took turns in addressing the gathering, and here are some quotes - VP Butt, “Thank you, to all who supported me. There is a lot to do and I will try to do my best to deliver what is expected." Secretary Wazid, “Thank you for your faith in me." Treasurer Rajpaul, "I hope that I am able to meet your expectations." Asst. Secretary/Treasurer Zamin Amin, “Thank you for electing me. It was not my desire to hold any position, but for the betterment of cricket, I will serve." President Rudy Persaud admitted that some mistakes were made by the previous administration, and as president he accepts the blame. He promised to rectify those issues and to be more forthright in his governance, adding "For this league to move forward, I need the help of all. Don't remain in the background and complain. Get involved and let us work together." I sat through the entire meeting and made a few observations, including how the delegates were very vocal in making their dissatisfaction known over the administration's failure to present a financial statement, among other issues alluded to in this report. Colin Sandy as the 2009 Vice President, was given an excellent "passing grade" for his work in and with the last administration, unfortunately, as previously stated, he was not returned to his post. With the exception of the Secretary and Treasurer, the other officers were elected by a 6-5 vote over their opponents. Strange? Were there two factions at the meeting? What do you think, I would like to know. Contact me at Ssamrajs@verizon.net

articles.excerpt: Queens Village achieved what some thought was beyond their grasps in 2009 - win a Triple Crown in the West Indian Softball Association. They did it with little or no expectation, a
articles.content:
Queens Village achieved what some thought was beyond their grasps in 2009 - win a Triple Crown in the West Indian Softball Association. They did it with little or no expectation, at least not from their competitors. The only Triple Crown talk in 2009 came from the much heralded Cornered Tigers Cricket Club who failed to win a single competition in 2009. They were WISA 2008 Triple Crown Champions. \[caption id="attachment\_418" align="alignright" width="500" caption="West Indian Softball Association triple crown champions Queens Village with their awards."\][![](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Queens_Village_2009_TripleCrownChamps2.jpg "Queens_Village_2009_TripleCrownChamps")

](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Queens_Village_2009_TripleCrownChamps2.jpg)\[/caption\] Queens Village narrowly edged out Ocean’s XI by six runs to win the WISA 20 Over Competition last Sunday at Dr. Charles Drew Park at Van Wyck and 115 Ave. That nerve wracking win allow them to complete the hat-trick of championships in 2009. Their first championship came at the expense of Sandals XI in early June. In that game, they crushed Sandals XI by 9 wickets to win the Div II 25 Over Championship. They followed that up with an upset of the ages by trashing their rival – Archer by 72 runs to take the Div I 30 Over Championship. How did the boys from Queens Village managed to accomplish their feat? Was it because they were under the radar for much of the season? Was it because no one expected anything of them? Was their competition not up to par? It had to be a combination of all and even more because none of the village boys wanted to comment. All they wanted to do was enjoy the moment and prepare for the competition in 2010. In the game played on Sunday Nov 15, 2009, Queens Village batted first and amassed a whopping 155 for 5 in their allotted 20 overs in blustery conditions. Their skipper D. Morgan top scored with 63 not out batting at number four. He was nicely supported by Haseeb Ally with 36. Bowling for Ocean’s XI, L Mohan (Jr) grabbed four of the five wickets that fell for twelve runs. The other wicket fell via the run out route. Asked to score at almost eight runs an over, Ocean’s XI had their work cut out for them. Nothing short of spectacular was required by Ocean’s XI to deny Queens Village CC a bid to win their first triple crown. Ocean’s XI started briskly but lost wickets in the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th overs before their captain L. Mohan and C. Rajbally brought some resistance to Queens Village’s bowlers. With the score at 30 for three at the end of four overs, Mohan and Rajbally played with a balance of caution and aggression. They took the score to 107 before Rajbally was out for 23 in the eleventh over. All Ocean’s XI needed to do from there was score 49 runs in eight overs with six wickets in hand. With some questionable gamesmanship from the village boys (not giving a runner to Mohan) and the ability to take wickets, Queens Village managed to bowl out Ocean’s XI for 149 in 18 overs, hence making them WISA 2009 Triple Crown Champions. L. Mohan who played like thee star he is top scored with 56. Ravi Parbhudial and R. Singh grabbed 3 for 27 and 3 for 24 respectively. Congratulations to Queens Village CC.

articles.title: Middlesex Subdue Diplomats On The Day Of Liberty
articles.excerpt: By Dyon Ravello Diplomats coming off two consecutive convincing victories found a challenge waiting when they met Middlesex at Marine Park C on Saturday, July 4th 2009. Mark Audain
articles.content:
By Dyon Ravello Diplomats coming off two consecutive convincing victories found a challenge waiting when they met Middlesex at Marine Park C on Saturday, July 4th 2009. Mark Audain won the toss and elected to field. Mark’s decision seemed faulty before he removed both openers in the sixth over, Former New York youth player Basdeo Ramnarine, caught and the veteran Oscar Prince, bowled, both batsmen falling with the score on 27. On the other end Mark’s son Dominic was firing on all cylinders with little returns. Audain senior continuing in the tenth over snared his third victim; Andre Kirton bowled to leave the Diplomats wobbling at 40 for 3. \[caption id="attachment\_133" align="alignright" width="237" caption="Casper Davis of Middlesex had figures for 5 for 22 against Diplomats."\][![](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Casper_Davis1-237x300.jpg "Casper_Davis1")

](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Casper_Davis1.jpg)\[/caption\] After 12 overs the slow bowlers were introduced as S. Ramphal, and S. Smith look to repair the damage, for the Diplomats. The pair added 33 before Ramphal gave catching practice to the fielder at backward point, off a long hop from Casper Davis, he made 20. Smith got hit on the knee roll and required a runner; he found Kirton, athletic and up to the task as Captain Simpson came to the crease. But Smith held out to Davis’ looping off breaks to depart for 25, and the Diplomats had dug themselves into a hole at 84 for 5 after 15 overs. D. Ravello saw Davis out after Smith’s dismissal and then took 9 runs of R Layne, to signal that surrender was not near. However, two overs later Layne’s off breaks similar to Davis’ picked up Simpson as he played a cheeky sweep to square leg, 100-6. Ravello stood in bewilderment as Keon Lake looped two whipped strokes in the air before Davis had him sky one to backward point, 105-7. Hubert Lewis joined Ravello and looked the part against the spin twin. However the reintroduction of speedster Dominic Audain saw Lewis’ stumps rattled by a brilliant Yorker. Ravello faced Dominic with confidence and charisma as he stuck his back foot into the onside before replacing it, to flash a short delivery to third man for four. Dominic’s last over costing 10. With the speed out of the way Ravello look to refocus along with Ray Joseph. But the hunting of Davis was always near. Davis’ first ball after the speedster got Joseph playing with a flat face to short extra cover. Ravello was now left with teenager Shane Smith to compose a competitive target. The inexperienced youth looked resilient until, Davis’ field change left the onside vastly open. Shane eyeing the acreage, heaved to finding welcoming hands at short square leg. Ravello stranded on 26, Diplomats 131 allout of 28 overs. Davis a former quick, finishing with 5 for 22 off 8 after Mark Audain began the rout with 3 for 22 of 6, Dominic 1 for 42 and Layne 1 for 23. Middlesex began the chase with all guns blazing, as Jacob Emmanuel, took to a liking for Ray Joseph. Emmanuel hit 3 fours and a 6 off Hubert Lewis on his way to 27. Emmanuel was caught on the mid wicket boundary the first ball Keon Lake had move to that position, a controversial moment since Lake held the ball immensely close to the ropes with Lewis gaining revenge for the maximum hit earlier. Ray Joseph bowled three over to concede 34 runs as the spins were introduced to stifle the run flow. Andre Kirton had D. Hector snatched at slip by Oscar Prince for 14 with 70 on the board after 10 overs. Lake bowling for the residential end was rewarded with a team scalp as C Lee was run out by Shane Smith 81-3. However the arrival of Casper Davis, who mixed a sound defense with well timed stroke play, ensured that this treaty was dead for the Diplomats. Davis saw the back of his Captain Mark Audain leg before to Kirton for 21. Davis saw Audain junior survive a scared as his pull to mid wicket was miss judged by Shane Smith in the Deep. But by this time the score had been settled. Simpson brought on himself and Ramphal the part time bowlers. Ramphal struck Davis’ pad to ensure that he did not see his team home, Davis made 21. In the end K. Mc Millan struck the winning runs, with Dominic not out on 21. Bowling for Diplomats, Lewis had 1 off 23 off 5, Ramphal 1 for 2 of 3 balls, and Kirton 2 for 26 of seven. Mark Audain and Casper Davis both performed with guile, on the day they won the game for Middlesex. Diplomats won on July 5th with Cavaliers forfeiting the game. This coming weekend, July 11th Diplomats after off, and can use the time vacation to tight the loose ends in the batting exposed by the Middlesex attack. A trip upstate is fitting to reset the momentum and treat the mind to a change in ambiance. On July 18 Diplomats look to rebound in the Brooklyn League when they host Jinnah at Marine Park C. Diplomats will be keen to improve on the 6-3-1 record which as seen them drop 4 winning percentage points for 71 to 67.

articles.excerpt: By Lloyd Jodah Exciting news came out of Dubai for USA Cricket, but it was not Twin colors in sport - USA and Afghanistan about the USA vs. Afghanistan match, it was about IPL Comm
articles.content: By Lloyd Jodah Exciting news came out of Dubai for USA Cricket, but it was not Twin colors in sport - USA and Afghanistan about the USA vs. Afghanistan match, it was about IPL Commissioner Lalit Modi meeting with USA Cricket's Don Lockerbie, Nabeel Ahmed and Ahmed Jeddy to discuss plans for the IPL in the United States, possibly as soon as 2011. That would be another huge positive leap for USA Cricket. On the field however the USA national team did not channel the enormous significance of playing against Afghanistan to put on a match-winning performance. Sometimes sports is not just a game; the New Orleans Saints’ road to Super Bowl XLIV was a daily beacon of hope and inspiration for the people of New Orleans, the State of Louisiana and the “Who Dat Nation.” The Saints found extra motivation to layer on their professionalism to win Super Bowl XLIV. Put in a "must-win" situation to continue to stand a chance to qualify for the T20 World Cup, the USA Team was also gifted with the additional motivation of playing the Afghans, but fell short. Afghanistan won the toss and decided to bat. Opening with spin, the USA’s Lennox Cush took the early wicket of Mohammed Shahzad but thereafter the Afghan batsmen all contributed, helped by dropped catches, misfielding and missed run out chances. Fielding takes on added importance in T20 cricket and can actually cost a team the match. Afghan opener Noor Ali scored 26 off 27 balls with 3 fours, Nowroz Mangal 30 in 27 balls with 3 fours, whilst the two not out batsmen were Mohammad Nabi 25\* in 18 balls with 2 fours and 1 six, and Raees Ahmadzai, 26 in 17 balls with 2 fours, along with Karim Sadiq, 25, helped Afghanistan reach 135 for 4 in 20 overs. A large media contingent was on hand to cover the game as interest in the match had been building for sometime in addition, some 1,000 Afghan supporters were in attendance to cheer the Cinderella team on. USA’s Carl Wright played a couple of good shots including a square drive for four and USA got to 28 after 7 overs before losing their first wicket, that of Sushil Nadkarni to pacer Ashraf for 12. Wright's 28 (2x4s) took 38 balls as the rest of the batsmen felt the pressure of the low scoring rate, with only Rashard Marshall 19 (2x4s) and Aditya Thyagarajan, 14, reached double figures. USA made 106 for 7 wickets in their 20 overs and never seriously challenged the 135 made by Afghanistan. Bowling for Afghanistan Hameed Hassan had his best T20 bowling figures of 4 overs,14 runs with 3 wickets. The 29-run defeat of the USA ensured Afghanistan a place in the Super Four Stage of the tournament.

articles.title: Massiah Needs To Call Time On U.s. T20 Career
articles.excerpt: By Orin Davidson Beset by a series of tactical blunders, the United States crashed out of the World Cup 20/20 qualifying competition, shattering hopes of a potential historic appea
articles.content:
By Orin Davidson Beset by a series of tactical blunders, the United States crashed out of the World Cup 20/20 qualifying competition, shattering hopes of a potential historic appearance in a prestigious Global championship. \[caption id="attachment\_91" align="alignright" width="400" caption="Steve Massiah is seen here pondering his next move in a New York Premier League game last year. Photo Zaheer Saffie."\][![](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Steve_Massiah10.jpg "Steve_Massiah")

](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/Steve_Massiah10.jpg)\[/caption\] Given the talent available in the squad, the team management badly misused its resources and emerged with two losses and one win. It proved inadequate to progress to the second round from which the top two of four teams would journey to the West Indies for the 2010 edition of the International Cricket Council’s second most important championship, after the 50 overs World Cup. In their defeats to Afghanistan and Scotland, the United States was guilty of poor team selection, bad use of bowlers and woeful batting order choices, that gifted their opponents victories that could’ve been denied with more thoughtful and objective decision making in the two main areas of the game. Against Ireland, the U.S. bowling let them down badly, allowing the former team to pile up a mammoth 202 runs tally, their highest score ever in 20 overs competition and so far the most conceded by any of the teams in UAE. With Ireland, rated the best team in the competition, and needing a victory to keep their hopes alive of qualifying, after losing their opening game to Afghanistan, they applied intense pressure from the get- go and the U.S. crumbled as a result with the captain Steve Massiah unable to counter Ireland’s early batting onslaught with his bowling tactics. There was an over-reliance on spin by Massiah who used four slow bowlers, a shocking tactic which allowed Ireland to feast for easy runs. In limited overs competition, the use of even one spinner is a risk, much less in 20/20 where the bowlers are attacked from ball one. Massiah committed suicide by giving Ireland 13 overs of spin of the allotted 20 and they capitalized fully, that initiated the beginning of the U.S’s ouster. With only three matches to qualify for the second round, the U.S. needed to play pressure cricket in all three games but they lowered their guard after defeating Scotland in the first game, where they used 11 overs of seam. They reduced that number in the next encounter and paid the penalty. The captain’s thinking was mind boggling because he had five seam bowlers in Kevin Darlington, Orlando Baker, Usman Shuja, Tim Allen and Rashard Marshall at his disposal, but chose only seven overs of the faster stuff, which is always more difficult to attack. To add insult to injury, Marshall is one of the country’s most effective seam bowlers, yet he was not given a single ball in all three matches. They chose to play him as a batsman, but these days Marshall has proven to be a better bowler, but the management was blind to this reality. Incredibly too, was the decision to use Tim Allen as a spinner when the player has been a specialist seamer all his career. There is a glaringly good reason why slow bowlers are never used by all teams at all levels of competition, at the death of an innings. If the team’s use of its bowlers was poor, its batting tactics were worst. Dhaniram who has failed every time he represented the U.S. as a batsman was inexplicably used in the top order. He never scored more than four runs in all three games, and even though he got a total of five in the two warm up games against the UAE, was still persisted with at number four and five thereafter. In contrast, Dhaniram has good results as a bowler and should’ve been used as a specialist spinner with no place for him batting in the top five. Why the decision makers could not have adjusted is beyond belief. At the same time, the team bewilderingly underused Aditha Thyagarajan, their best batsman from the Americas Championships one year ago. A shocking omission from the first game, Thayagrajan was only drafted in for the second encounter because Sushil Nadkarnie was unfit. To make matters worse he was used at number seven in the order and promptly exposed the mistake by slamming an accomplished 72, not out, by far the highest for any U.S. player. Then, to rub salt in the wounds, the team failed to promote him next game in the crucial run chase against Afghanistan, keeping him at number seven which was much too late. With all of these factors staring the team management in the face, they still regarded Dhaniram a batsman. And to crown a dreadfully mismanaged campaign, Massiah failed to lead from the front even though he is supposed to be the team’s premier batsman. The captain has scored all of his many runs for the team at number three, yet he dropped himself down the order when the team needed him most in all three games. Against Afghanistan he appeared as a tail ender at number eight. And the fact that he never scored more than five runs in the three competition games and a total of 13 in the two warm-up matches, raises serious doubts about his future in the team for 20/20 matches. Massiah is accustomed to having his way in almost all team matters whether it is team selection, batting order placements or tactics on the field. And unless there was a steep change of team policy, the disastrous showing of the US team in the Middle East has justified the critics claim that he has no place in the 20/20 team. If there was no change in that policy, then coach Clayton Lambert’s position should also be in jeopardy as those tactical blunders were inexcusable. Significantly, by getting dumped in the first round, the U.S. failed to justify the ICC wildcard entry it received for this competition to the annoyance of other teams. Massiah is more comfortable in the 50 overs version as a batsman and should remain there in the U.S. team setup. Ricky Ponting, has relinquished his place in the game’s shortest version for Australia and so has Andrew Strauss for England. Therefore, there is no humiliation in the U.S. captain following suit, given his shortcomings. And any explanations of the U.S. losing to better equipped teams would not wash with anyone. Does Afghanistan, a war thorn country, among others, have superior facilities, better domestic competitions or better coaches?

articles.excerpt: By Linden Dodson In Washington last summer something great occurred in a cricket tournament that \[caption id="attachment\74" align="alignright" width="500" caption="The victorious
articles.content:
By Linden Dodson In Washington last summer something great occurred in a cricket tournament that \[caption id="attachment\_74" align="alignright" width="500" caption="The victorious NY region team."\][![](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/New_York_eastern_Conference_team3.jpg "New_York_eastern_Conference_team")

](http://www.newyorkcricket.com/v2/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/New_York_eastern_Conference_team3.jpg)\[/caption\] will affect all involved for a life time. After two days of cricket in the Eastern Conference Tournament hosted by Atlantic Region, a star studded New York Region Team was reduced to third place behind Atlantic Region who had won both of their games and South East Region who had beaten New York and Lost to Atlantic Region.  The team management, Linden Frazier (Coach), Steve Massiah (Captain) and yours truly (Manager) decided to forgo meeting with the team that Saturday evening scheduling instead a team meeting for 8.00 am on Sunday. Our last game, against Atlantic Region, the front runners was scheduled for 10.00 am on Sunday. The meeting was held at the hotel, right after breakfast, in the court yard, in the morning sunshine where we could find some privacy. At the meeting the team was apprised of the situation and the numbers were explained; we had worked out a chart and graph in which the most likely scenarios were extrapolated this was communicated to the team; the boys were then challenged individually and as a team to go out and make New York proud. The rest is history New York dismissed Atlantic region for 82 in 32 overs then responded with 84 in 9.3 overs; by 1:30 pm on Sunday the game was over. New York catapulted from third place to first place in two hours of breath taking cricket. In Dubai this week Team USA found themselves in the same scenario in the Twenty 20 World Cup qualifiers. After two days of cricket they were third place and needed to overcome a net run rate deficit of 2.6 runs per over to beat Afghanistan and qualify for the Super Four. Afghanistan batted first (good for the USA position) and compiled 135 for 4 in their allotted 20 overs therefore USA need 136 in 14.5 overs to go to the next round they could only muster 106 for 7 in their turn at the wicket. Is it possible that the details were not communicated to the team and they were not fired up to go out and achieve as was done in Washington? In New York the sacking of the Manager and Coach without explanation was well ventilated and it was brought out at that time that Massiah was part of the process that removed the Manager and Coach. It should be now very clear to all that neither Massiah nor the administration valued the part that motivation and inspiration played in winning. Cricket was sacrificed at the altar of politics. The Afghan medium pace bowler Hamid Hassan said in the post match interview that he enjoys looking at USA television and movies and particularly he liked Rocky and his team is the “Rocky” of International Cricket. Twenty two year old Hasan took eleven wickets in the tournament including three against USA. The difference between the two teams is obvious the Afghans had bigger dreams and younger legs they were able to take inspiration from an American folk hero to beat America while team USA saw no value in such trivialities. The two teams that emerged from the ICC Twenty20 qualifiers and will participate in the ICC World Twenty20 this spring in the West Indies are Afghanistan and Ireland. For the record, let it be known that the average age of the Afghans is 22 years old; their youngest player is 17 years old and their captain is 25 years old. By the same token the average age of the Irelanders is 25 years old; their youngest player is 17 years old and their captain is 25 years old.  Compare this to Team USA with 10 players over 30 years old including Dhaniram (9 runs from 5 innings) 43 years old. After the tournament Americans in Dubai were left with the impression that in New York and USA cricket there are no big dreams and young legs. USA cricketers, spectators and most stake-holders know otherwise and we must wash shame out of our eyes and demand nothing but the best from those who represent us on and off the field. We the people understand that A New York under 25 Team or better still a USA under 25 Team, Coach Frazier (New York) and / or Coach Benjamin (California) with a Manager who can motivate and inspire would defeat both Ireland and Afghanistan.
